title: Holdback Carried by a Vehicle with Faults Standing since Its Last Inspection
content:
The valuation the marketplace records is fixed only after every fault the vehicle's condition record has been advised of stands on that record as a fault report of its own.

Where a Keyturn Vehicle Listing carries fault reports that postdate its last completed inspection, the vehicle carries a holdback, and the size of it turns on how many such reports stand in the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date.

- A vehicle carrying three or more fault reports in that window, the most recent of them dated later than its last completed inspection, carries a holdback of six hundredths (0.06).
- A vehicle carrying one or two such reports in that window with the most recent dated later than its last completed inspection carries a holdback of three hundredths (0.03).
- Any other vehicle carries no holdback on this ground, a holdback rate of 0.

### Points of judgement

*What the second condition asks.* Both of the first two clauses require the most recent fault report to be dated later than the last completed inspection. A vehicle carrying five fault reports in the window, all of them predating its last completed inspection, carries no holdback on this ground.

*Where the count divides.* At 3 fault reports in the window the first clause governs; at 2 the second does. A vehicle with no fault report in the window is on the last clause.

*The window.* The rolling twelve months are counted back from the handling date, so a fault report dated fourteen months back is not counted, however recent it is against the last inspection.
